result.summary: This PR adds a new AssertUnreachable() macro that directly calls the noreturn assertion_fail() helper, and mechanically replaces assert(false)/Assert(false)-style unreachable-code assertions across nearly the entire codebase with it. It also adds util/check.h includes wherever Assert/assert is used (to keep the project's no-NDEBUG guarantee visible) and adds two new linters (assert_falsy, std_unreachable) to enforce the pattern going forward. The bulk of the diff (312 files) is mechanical scripted-diff churn following from this single utility change.
result.problem: Existing falsy assertions are ambiguous about whether NDEBUG can disable them, and Assert(false) can trigger GCC return-type warnings because the noreturn attribute is hidden behind a function call; developers maintaining any part of the codebase hit this confusion. The fix is purely a utils/build-hygiene change, not tied to any specific area's user-facing behavior.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp: AssertUnreachable pulls in assertion_fail from util/check.cpp, which libbitcoin_consensus (crypto-only in principle) should not depend on; the riscv job links it standalone and breaks. Author acknowledged and said they'll fix before taking the PR out of draft, but has not yet done so.
resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp: the assert_falsy regex missed variants like 'assert (false)' or 'assert(0&&"x")'; author adopted the suggested stricter regex.
jeanpablojp: the linter-adding commit was ordered before the scripted-diff that satisfies it, breaking CI mid-series; author swapped the commit order.

result.card: This PR adds a new AssertUnreachable() macro to util/check.h and mechanically replaces assert(false)-style unreachable-code assertions across 312 files, plus adds two new linters (assert_falsy, std_unreachable) to enforce the pattern. It solves a build-hygiene confusion (NDEBUG semantics, GCC return-type warnings from Assert(false) hiding noreturn) for anyone maintaining the codebase, not a specific user-facing area. It is draft, needs rebase, and CI is failing; reviewer jeanpablojp found real implementation issues (regex gaps, commit ordering, and a libbitcoin_consensus/util linkage break on riscv), two of which the author fixed while the third remains open with the author committing to fix it before marking ready. No one has objected to the underlying change. Almost all of the huge diff is mechanical call-site churn following from the new macro, so only utils and tests (for the new linters) are treated as substantive category members.
